Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a settlement that delivers direct, automatic payments to the identified class and avoids a claims process. The proposal also ensures any fee amount the court declines to award benefits the class. We are prepared to discuss the terms.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to provide substantial, direct relief to the identified class, but the proposed total exceeds its authorized settlement range. Our counteroffer is $33 million for the class and $6 million in attorneys’ fees, with automatic distribution. The fee remains subject to court approval; Brightline will not agree to clear sailing, and any unawarded fee amount will revert to Brightline. Total cash outlay would be $39 million.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the automatic distribution and the absence of clear sailing. Our counter keeps the fee request subject to court approval and asks that any amount not awarded benefit the class rather than return to Brightline.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We propose a substantial, certain recovery for the class, with direct payment to identified members and no claims barrier. The fee request is separate from class relief and remains subject to the Court’s independent review.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: Brightline cannot accept the proposed terms because their total cash outlay exceeds its authorized limit. We are evaluating a counterproposal and remain open to discussing a resolution within that limit.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We are prepared to make a substantial movement from our opening position to facilitate resolution. Our counter preserves direct, automatic payments to identified members and ensures any fee not approved by the Court benefits the class. If this remains above Brightline’s authority, please identify the range it can support so we can focus further discussions.

private_notes.private_reasoning: The class has a meaningful but uncertain trial recovery, with additional certification risk and delay. Identifiable members make automatic distribution important. Open with a substantial but negotiable class fund and keep any court-declined fee amount for the class rather than Brightline.

The class has substantial merits leverage, but certification risk and a 2–3 year path to trial warrant a practical settlement posture. Open with a strong class recovery and insist on automatic payments because Brightline can identify every member. Keep fees separate from the class fund, avoid clear sailing, and direct any court-disallowed fee amount to the class rather than Brightline.

Do not accept either opening demand: Hargrove's total is $43.2 million, above the authorized cap, and Whitcombe's is $50 million. Make one complete, below-cap counteroffer to Hargrove, preserving automatic payments while limiting total cash outlay to $39 million. Avoid a simultaneous proposal to Whitcombe that could create competing binding obligations; keep that channel open without making an offer.

The defense offer provides substantial, certain, automatic relief, but I should use an early round to seek a better class outcome without sacrificing the valuable automatic distribution. The firm has no personal financial incentive to maximize fees. I will keep fees at the defense’s proposed amount and seek a modest increase to the class fund plus reversion of any unawarded fees to the class.

The initial $50 million total demand exceeded Brightline’s stated authority. With no counteroffer or disclosed cap, move materially while preserving meaningful, certain class relief. Prioritize automatic payments and ensure any fee the Court does not award benefits the class rather than Brightline. A $25 million fund plus a proportionate $6.25 million fee is a substantial but more realistic counter; do not accept a nonexistent defense term sheet.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP’s latest proposal has a $31.25 million total cash outlay, below Brightline’s $40 million cap and lower than Hargrove Lane LLP’s proposal. It includes automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and puts unawarded fees toward the class. Accepting it secures a binding settlement on the lower-cost terms.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties negotiated a settlement providing a $25,000,000 class fund, $6,250,000 in attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to Court approval, no clear-sailing agreement, and automatic distribution to identified class members. Class counsel’s opening proposal was $40,000,000 for the class and $10,000,000 in fees, with automatic payments and any unawarded fee benefiting the class. After Brightline stated that the proposal exceeded its authorized limit, class counsel proposed the settlement terms now reached. The class-fund and fee amounts were included together in the proposals; they were not negotiated only after class relief had been agreed. The Court retains independent authority to determine the fee, and any amount not awarded will benefit the class.
